prompts.referenceRole: The user attachment is visual inspiration for goofy simple cartoon proportions only; create new duck designs.
prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: a polished tabletop board-game player-token design sheet, FOUR physical duck tiles, not a screen or sprite sheet.
Input image: visual inspiration ONLY for flat goofy cartoon duck proportions, big humorous bill and simple friendly eye. Invent original distinctive ducks; do not trace its outline or reproduce its pose.
On a plain warm ivory tabletop, show four separate thick die-cut cardboard DUCK SILHOUETTE TILES in a spacious 2 by 2 arrangement, all equal game-piece footprint. Every tile is a flat printed face with a neat cream cut edge following a compact duck silhouette, a very thin visible layered-cardboard bevel and a short subtle contact shadow. Mostly overhead so the printed art is seen clearly. These are tangible chunky board-game pieces that can be picked up, not living birds, figurines or loose illustrations.
Art: playful clean flat cartoon shapes, confident dark ink accents, huge funny orange bills, expressive offset eyes, amusing individual personalities, restrained two-tone shading, no feather detail, no painterly fur, no anime sparkle. Compact chubby body and head read as one tile; feet and neck do not make fragile narrow cutout pieces. Print fills the tile with a small consistent edge.
Four player identities distinguishable by BOTH colour and duck design: teal-headed warm-brown mallard with a cheeky raised brow; buttery yellow round duck with a single wonky head tuft and surprised face; coral/rust duck with cream cheek patches and a wide pleased grin; violet/slate duck with pale breast and a small swept-back crest, gently deadpan. All equally appealing, same illustration family, equal visual weight. Colour is built into their plumage and wings, not merely a coloured circle behind the same duck.
Composition: four hero tiles only, large and fully visible, generous separation and margin, landscape sheet. No headings, text, numbers, logos, UI, rewards, decorative scenery, extra sample objects or circular coin mounts. The image should immediately say funny tactile tabletop components.

Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: original seed-encounter tile concept sheet for the same goofy cartoon duck tabletop game.
Show THREE alternative seed-category game tiles arranged across a warm ivory tabletop, large and equally spaced. Each is clearly a flat, thick die-cut printed cardboard token: crisp thin cream cut rim, subtle layered edge, tiny natural contact shadow, face nearly square to overhead camera. These are manufactured tabletop components, not scattered real seeds, buttons, jewels or glossy mobile-game icons.
Shared face art on all three: a bold playful illustration of THREE chunky golden sunflower-type seeds, simple warm ochre/caramel shapes with one dark centre mark and minimal two-tone shading, clear dark teal ink contours. Flat friendly cartoon illustration, very few lines, readable at small board-game sizes. All use the same pale warm face colour, orange accent edge and consistent illustration size.
Explore three deliberate OUTER TILE SILHOUETTES for the seed encounter category, left to right: a softly rounded triangular tile inspired by a little cluster of seeds; a compact smooth asymmetric seed/teardrop-shaped tile; a softly rounded hexagonal tile. Each silhouette is broad and touch friendly, not sharp, elaborate or cut around every illustrated seed. Faces should have a small unobtrusive blank cream area near the lower edge where a strength numeral could be printed later; NO numeral or text in this concept. These are shape alternatives for ONE category, not different values or additional powers.
Composition: one clean landscape concept sheet, three tiles only, fully visible margins. Tactile cardboard edges are visible but artwork stays flat and graphic. No text, captions, numbers, logos, duck characters, hands, board, decorative seeds outside the tokens, photorealistic seed detail or painterly highlights.

prompts.role: Illustrated board with three connected biomes
prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: the actual illustrated cardboard BOARD for an original goofy cartoon duck tabletop game. Landscape 3:2 composition, directly overhead; entire single board with rounded outer corners, thin tangible cardboard edge and tiny shadow on neutral ivory table. Art fills the board, no app interface, panels or score dashboard.
Primary composition: THREE distinct connected biomes occupying approximately equal areas from left to right. One continuous broad clearly traceable footpath winds into one generous horseshoe-like open loop in each biome, with TWO obvious wooden bridges connecting adjacent biomes. The bridge at the first region boundary leads only to the second region, the next only to the third. This is a single journey with a start and an end, not three separate closed racetracks; no route forks, crossing paths or shortcuts. Keep the full path visible and open for game tokens.
First biome: a welcoming blue duck pond, soft spring grass and reeds, a quiet inviting beginning near the pond. Ordinary path stopping patches look modest but comfortable.
Middle biome: a richer, lush green meadow/grove with flowering shrubs, shade and many inviting resting places along the path: sheltered grassy hollows, a nest under a bush, a cosy log nook. The most welcoming overall region, clearly more abundant and comfortable.
Final biome: a visibly barren windswept ochre and dusty-mauve wasteland, sparse dead grass and cracked dry earth, humorous rather than frightening. Most path places are exposed and poor resting ground. Place TWO rare exceptionally snug refuges directly on this final path: a lush sheltered spring beneath a rock overhang, and a deeply cushioned leafy hollow sheltered from wind. They should stand out as little treasures of comfort in an otherwise harsh landscape.
The winding path must be an integral part of the painted board. Indicate a sequence of organic irregular footprint-sized stopping patches using earth, flat stones, grass clearings and sandy patches. Some stopping patches widen into the illustrated rest places above, WITHIN the main route rather than on separate branches. Use natural changes of surface/edging to show where tokens could sit. Do not use rows of rigid circles, numbered discs, dotted circles, arrows or UI overlays. Keep footprints and rests reasonably similar in scale so a physical tile could fit; the exact indexed-space count will be mapped later, this is an art concept, not a final numbered rules board.
Art direction: charming original flat cartoon board-game illustration, rounded chunky shapes, confident dark warm-teal contour accents, warm clear colour blocks, minimal graphic shading, playful simplified scenery matching a goofy wide-billed cartoon duck token. Crisp, appealing professionally printed tabletop art; no realistic textures, painterly fantasy rendering or videogame 3D scene. Terrain edges blend naturally while the bridges make biome transitions obvious.
Leave the route empty of player pieces to show the board design clearly. No ducks, extra character cameos, reward icons, numerical values, text, logos, title, legends, buttons, inset panels or separate little boards. The environment communicates modest comfort, plentiful comfort, then rare comfort amid adversity.
